To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) firm productivity increases and financial frictions reduce GVC participation of firms, (2) the effect of productivity on GVC participation is similar for firms that have been exporting continuously and those that have just entered the market, while the effect of financial frictions is only significant for the latter, and (3) the negative effect of financial constraints on GVC participation dampens the positive effect of firm productivity.
productivity and financial factors affect firms' GVC integration, but the effects are not uniform for different firms.

Productivity increases and financial constraints decrease the extent of global value chain participation of exporting firms, and the effect of financial constraints on global value chain participation is more pronounced for first time exporters than for continuous exporters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of productivity and financial constraints in the GVC literature and contributes to the empirical literature on the heterogeneous firm model.
the following question: what determines Chinese firms' participation in GVC?

the following questions: How does the productivity of firms affect their GVC participation? Does the financial status of firms influence their participation in the GVC? And, does the productivity of the firms affect their GVP participation differently in the presence of different financial status?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GVC participation of Chinese exporters is positively related with firm productivity and negatively related with financial constraints.
productivity and financial factors are both important in determining firms' value chain participation.
productivity and financial constrains both play an important role in determining firms' global value added ratio.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
financial constraints are an important determinant of firms' GVC integration and the effect of financial constraints on GVC participation is heterogeneous among exporters.
financial constraints can affect firms' GVC decisions by influencing their productivity, and that financial constraints can reduce the effect of productivity on GVC decisions.

financial development facilitates firms' participation in GVCs by reducing financial constraints, which in turn promotes productivity growth and enhances the efficiency of resource allocation in the economy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
financial constraints may be an important factor in explaining the GVC participation of firms in developing countries.
financial constraints may hinder the GVC participation of firms with high productivity.
financial constraints may be a major reason for China's low GVC participation.
